Calculate amateur batting statistics across games

Source: R/calculate_youth_stats.R
calculate_youth_stats.Rd

Summarize each player's scored games with statistics suited to amateur and youth baseball, where fielding errors are common and samples are small. Includes on-base percentage with errors (OBPE), isolated power, strikeout and walk rates, and batting average on balls in play.

Usage

calculate_youth_stats(scorecards, by = c("player", "game"), min_pa = 25)

Arguments

scorecards

A data frame with the seven columns returned by import_scorecards() or daimond_games(). All entries must be reviewed (needs_review = FALSE) with known confidence.

by

"player" (default) to pool each player's games within a team, or "game" for one row per game, team, and player.

min_pa

Nonnegative whole number. Rows with fewer plate appearances are marked small_sample = TRUE. The default, 25, is a rule of thumb, not a statistical threshold.

Value

One row per team and player (plus game_id when by = "game"), in first-appearance order, with counting columns G, PA, AB, H, HR, ROE, BB, HBP, SO, SF, TB; rate columns OBP, OBPE, ISO, K_rate, BB_rate, BABIP; and logical small_sample. Zero denominators produce NA_real_.

Details

Formulas:

  • OBP = (H + BB + HBP) / (AB + BB + HBP + SF)

  • OBPE = (H + BB + HBP + ROE) / (AB + BB + HBP + SF), where ROE counts plays scored as error. Errors are an out the defense failed to make, so in youth games OBPE shows how often a batter puts pressure on the defense. The idea follows McBride (UC Irvine 2025), who reports that on-base with errors predicted youth scoring better than standard OBP; the exact formula here is this package's definition.

  • ISO = (TB - H) / AB, extra bases per at-bat.

  • K_rate = SO / PA and BB_rate = (BB, including intentional) / PA.

  • BABIP = (H - HR) / (AB - SO - HR + SF).

Pooling with by = "player" matches players by exact team and player name, so the same name on two teams stays separate, and spelling must be consistent across scorecards. Automatic-runner and blank markers are not plate appearances. Quality at-bats need pitch-by-pitch counts, which paper scorecard cells do not record, so they are not calculated.

References

UC Irvine School of Social Sciences. 2025. "Coaching Youth Baseball and Softball with Sabermetrics." March 11. https://www.socsci.uci.edu/newsevents/news/2025/2025-03-11-mcbride-sabermetrics.php.

See also

calculate_batting_stats() for per-game BA, SLG, and OPS.

Examples

youth <- calculate_youth_stats(reviewed_scorecards)
head(youth[order(-youth$OBPE), c("team", "player", "PA", "OBP", "OBPE")])
#>                    team          player PA  OBP OBPE
#> 43        New York Mets     Bo Bichette  5 0.80 0.80
#> 2  Arizona Diamondbacks Geraldo Perdomo  4 0.75 0.75
#> 7  Arizona Diamondbacks   Jordan Lawlar  4 0.50 0.50
#> 8  Arizona Diamondbacks     Pavin Smith  4 0.50 0.50
#> 12  St. Louis Cardinals   Alec Burleson  4 0.50 0.50
#> 15  St. Louis Cardinals      Masyn Winn  4 0.50 0.50
